title: The Merons of the Universe
deck:
Merons are ordered cuboctahedral organizations of Compalphas whose
            geometry, growth, and interaction define the different simple
            substances in the Meronic Model.

concise.body:
Merons

In this chapter, we demonstrate the true forms of the structural elements that are referred to in conventional physical and chemical sciences as "atoms," along with their true mechanisms of interaction.

If we analyze all known chemical elements, both natural and artificial, we can establish through practical means that hydrogen is the simplest, lightest, and most abundant of all.

This microscopic corpuscular system is functionally equivalent to any macroscopic planetary system, such as our solar system. In reality, according to TUIDG, hydrogen—here called the Metalpha Meron—is constituted not by three "masses," but by twelve Compalphas, with each Compalpha consisting of six types of Intrinsic Magnetic Fields (six types of concentric toroidal forms) made of "immaterial lines of force," or more accurately, Interaction Circles.

The geometric structure described is, in conventional physical terms, the logical substitute for the illogical "proton," the unnecessary "neutron," and the impossible "electron" all at once.

TUIDG’s Merons, like the atoms of the traditional physical-chemical model, are structures composed of smaller parts; however, these parts are not necessarily substantial, but merely parts of a larger geometry.

The designation of Merons applies to the set of all existing types of chemical elements or simple substances, including those called isotopes, isotones, and isobars—all qualitative equivalents of what modern science calls atoms. In this way, the Merons are named in increasing order: Metalpha (met = 1; hydrogen); Etalpha (et = 2; deuterium); Propalpha (prop = 3; tritium), and so on.

Tabela xx - The name of the Merons

The Meronic growth sequence is formed by ordered linkages of Cuboctahedra (Metalpha Merons), and such linkages occur via the four Alpha Triads of each Cuboctahedron. In Animation 6.2, we can observe how two Metalpha Merons link, via the Alpha Triads (a triangular face of the cube), to form the Etalpha Meron.

Each Cuboctahedron added to the pre-existing Meronic structure produces a new type of Meron. Consequently, a vast number of stable Merons may exist, forming other types of simple substances in the superheated, supercompact centers of stars, while only about 266 types exist under the mild temperature and pressure conditions prevalent on the rocky and gaseous planets surrounding these stars.

In regions of space where pressure is extremely intense, such as the centers of stars, Merons with colossal structures—on the scale of planets—can exist. Through an understanding of the Geometric Continuum geometry, we see that these gigantic Merons possess the form of a Cuboctahedron, which, not coincidentally, is the structural form of the Metacube Meron or Metalpha (Hydrogen-1)—a reduction of the Geometric Continuum structure to its unit cell.

According to the structural properties of Merons—factoring in gravity, pressure, and temperature—we can hypothesize that all stars in the universe possess a kind of solid body in their interior.

According to TUIDG, each of the approximately 266 stable Merons is not merely numerically different but also structurally distinct. Simple substances are formed by identical or different sets of Merons—usually two or three types—that combine their individual characteristics to form the approximately 112 to 120 simple substances described by conventional chemistry; they are sets of distinct elements. Animation 6.2 demonstrates how the first 12 Cuboctahedra are added in the Meronic construction process of the first 12 Merons.

full.body:
Merons

Animation 6 - The Geometric Structure of Meron Metalpha

In this chapter, we demonstrate the true forms of the structural elements that are referred to in conventional physical and chemical sciences as "atoms," along with their true mechanisms of interaction. Such elements, in this theory, are called Merons, a composition of the Greek word meros (meaning "part" or "portion") and the suffix "-on," designating functionality—a functional part, a functional component. The term Meron (pl. Merons) is, therefore, a logical and non-contradictory way to name the true components of that which we understand to be "matter," but which, in reality, are merely "immaterial geometric elements."

If we analyze all known chemical elements, both natural and artificial, we can establish through practical means that hydrogen is the simplest, lightest, and most abundant of all. However, according to TUIDG, we see that it cannot logically be constituted by a trio of supposed "quarks," joined by a cloud of supposed "gluons," and orbited by a supposed "electron" linked to this trio by a cloud of supposed "photons." The problem with this corpuscular model, according to the logic governing Newton's third law (the principle of action and reaction), is that this system—lacking direct contact between its countless particles—cannot interact in a way that provides any type of "essentially attractive" mechanism. The logic governing Coulomb's law cannot function within these supposed "corpuscles" separated by vast empty spaces. There is no mechanism that provides any type of functional stability. In a corpuscular system such as this, the only law that truly holds is Newton's third law.

This microscopic corpuscular system is functionally equivalent to any macroscopic planetary system, such as our solar system. The problem, however, is that if gravitation cannot be explained in terms of mediating particles, why should the forces of the microcosm be valid for the same mechanism of action, given that the only difference between these two systems of bodies relates solely to the Structural Dimension to which they belong? Would the "size" of a system be capable of completely changing its fundamental mechanism of interaction? No. In reality, according to TUIDG, hydrogen—here called the Metalpha Meron—is constituted not by three "masses," but by twelve Compalphas, with each Compalpha consisting of six types of Intrinsic Magnetic Fields (six types of concentric toroidal forms) made of "immaterial lines of force," or more accurately, Interaction Circles. Thus, twelve Compalphas, joined in a functionally logical manner according to the principle of Rotating Interaction, form the structure of the Metalpha Meron.

The geometric structure described is, in conventional physical terms, the logical substitute for the illogical "proton," the unnecessary "neutron," and the impossible "electron" all at once. Their "positive" and "neutral" aspects are defined solely by the way their Compalphas are linked via their "north and south" poles. The aspect of the "electron" arises from the action-at-a-distance of the Compalphas' own Interaction Circles, where their radius of action—the point at which we could "find" two shared electrons from two atoms—is defined by the material's average density, and therefore by the inter-meronic (interatomic) distance in its various physical states.

TUIDG’s Merons, like the atoms of the traditional physical-chemical model, are structures composed of smaller parts; however, these parts are not necessarily substantial, but merely parts of a larger geometry. According to TUIDG, the word Meron (pl. Merons) is the most appropriate designation for the constituent parts of apparent substance, since the non-divisibility of anything whatsoever is impossible. Physics truly requires a revision of concepts, as the name "atom" (meaning "indivisible") contradicts the investigative spirit of particle physics, which demonstrates the practically indefinite divisibility of such a structure. The name Meron is a composition of the Greek word meros ("part, portion, segment") and the letter "n," which provides emphasis to the concept of a functional part, much like the final "n" in "neutron."

The designation of Merons applies to the set of all existing types of chemical elements or simple substances, including those called isotopes, isotones, and isobars—all qualitative equivalents of what modern science calls atoms. Thus, one could quite aptly call them, for example, "Hydrogen Meron," "Helium Meron," and so on, instead of "Hydrogen atom," "Helium atom," etc. However, the proper name of each Meron derives from or alludes to the nomenclature of organic chemistry, combining Greek prefixes corresponding to the number of carbons present in hydrocarbon molecules, with the distinction that instead of carbon "atoms," we account for the Cuboctahedra that form the Meronic structure. In this way, the Merons are named in increasing order: Metalpha (met = 1; hydrogen); Etalpha (et = 2; deuterium); Propalpha (prop = 3; tritium), and so on.

Tabela xx - The name of the Merons

The Meronic growth sequence is formed by ordered linkages of Cuboctahedra (Metalpha Merons), and such linkages occur via the four Alpha Triads of each Cuboctahedron. The Cuboctahedra fit together perfectly, like pieces of a puzzle, by means of their triangular faces to form the different types of Merons. Each Cuboctahedron can bind to a maximum of four other Cuboctahedra due to the synchronous order of the Rotating Interaction; otherwise, this rotational synchronism would be broken. In Animation 6.2, we can observe how two Metalpha Merons link, via the Alpha Triads (a triangular face of the cube), to form the Etalpha Meron.

Each Cuboctahedron added to the pre-existing Meronic structure produces a new type of Meron. Consequently, a vast number of stable Merons may exist, forming other types of simple substances in the superheated, supercompact centers of stars, while only about 266 types exist under the mild temperature and pressure conditions prevalent on the rocky and gaseous planets surrounding these stars.

In regions of space where pressure is extremely intense, such as the centers of stars, Merons with colossal structures—on the scale of planets—can exist. Through an understanding of the Geometric Continuum geometry, we see that these gigantic Merons possess the form of a Cuboctahedron, which, not coincidentally, is the structural form of the Metacube Meron or Metalpha (Hydrogen-1)—a reduction of the Geometric Continuum structure to its unit cell. Note that this refers to the unit cell rather than the unit element; there is a distinction between these two structures: the unit element is the Compalpha, while the unit cell is the Cuboctahedron.

According to the structural properties of Merons—factoring in gravity, pressure, and temperature—we can hypothesize that all stars in the universe possess a kind of solid body in their interior. Stars are not merely "balls of gas"; they contain solid structures that may eventually suffer ruptures and disintegrations, causing them to float in the more rarefied layers of the star. Such "crystals" could behave like fragments or shards of magnetized diamond floating on the stellar surface. The Meronic growth process differs from the description of conventional atomic growth, where stability is achieved only when a specific number of neutrons are added relative to a specific number of protons as the "atom" becomes more massive, with physical and chemical characteristics defined solely by electric charges.

According to TUIDG, each of the approximately 266 stable Merons is not merely numerically different but also structurally distinct. These structural differences are precisely what are responsible for the physical and chemical characteristics of different simple substances. It is important to note the distinction between distinct Merons and simple substances: a Meron is any distinct set of Cuboctahedra strongly linked by Alpha Triads via Meronic Circles, forming a continuous block or cluster of these cubes—a particular element. Simple substances are formed by identical or different sets of Merons—usually two or three types—that combine their individual characteristics to form the approximately 112 to 120 simple substances described by conventional chemistry; they are sets of distinct elements. Animation 6.2 demonstrates how the first 12 Cuboctahedra are added in the Meronic construction process of the first 12 Merons.
